facts.text: Mora was formally founded as a Hispanic farming community after Mexican independence, on a land grant issued September 28, 1835, by Governor Albino Pérez.
The town’s name comes from the Mora family, not from mulberry trees, despite the Spanish word “mora” meaning “mulberry.”.
Two short battles of the Mexican–American War were fought in Mora in 1847, ending the Taos Revolt.
The Mora Land Grant originally covered over 800,000 acres but was fragmented by the early 1900s, leaving heirs with about 60,000 acres by 1910.
Missionary activity remained minimal in Mora, with Franciscan visits limited to transients because the region’s remoteness deterred intensive evangelization.
The Mora Valley saw initial Spanish exploration in the 18th century as a passage for expeditions, but permanent settlements did not appear until the late 1700s.
